description_full: Teck Resources Limited engages in research, exploration, development, processing, smelting, refining, and reclamation of mineral properties in Asia, the Americas, and Europe. It operates through Copper and Zinc segments. The company offers copper, zinc, and lead concentrates, as well as refined zinc, lead, and silver. It also produces lead, precious metals, molybdenum, fertilizers, and other metals; and sells refined metals or concentrates. In addition, it explores for gold. The company was formerly known as Teck Cominco Limited and changed its name to Teck Resources Limited in April 2009. Teck Resources Limited was founded in 1913 and is based in Vancouver, Canada.

financial_summary: Teck Resources Ltd is a large-cap basic materials business with a $26.5B market cap on $7.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -17% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 34%.
The company is burning through $252M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.8% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 46% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 23% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 26% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 49% and a beta of 1.11, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.93 vs 5y 1.16), so read it loosely.

The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 18%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $11.02 to $78.49 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.

Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 379% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of -1.0% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 4 covering analysts target $55.12 on average, 2% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 8% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.1%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.95).
It runs a 34% gross margin and burns cash (FCF margin -3%).
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.38x.
ROE of 4% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $777.8M.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.74 in the distress zone.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -16.7% over 3 years and 2.9% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 30%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 39.3% on average.
Analysts expect -16.2% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.8%, and institutions hold 77%.
It returns 3.3% a year to shareholders (2.6% in buybacks and 0.6% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 1.7% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 16 consecutive years, raising it 17.4% a year over the last five.

Free cash flow is negative, at -$34K per employee.
CEO pay is $3.2M (3x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (9/10, lower is better).
